headline: High-risk pair: caveman’s MCP/file-writing content workflow can feed Haystack’s broad-egress retrieval stack, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP, and caveman reads/writes files like CLAUDE.md, project notes, and memory files while Haystack can consume MCP servers. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path through shared content, though no shared filesystem is explicitly documented, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF caveman writes attacker-controlled text into CLAUDE.md or project notes and Haystack ingests that content via MCP
IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server or shared workspace without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable MCP on one side for the shared workflow
Restrict Haystack to allowlisted MCP servers only
Separate caveman notes from any Haystack-ingested directory
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent content
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization before MCP ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Haystack has broad network egress and REST/MCP interfaces. If caveman content reaches Haystack, sensitive local artifacts can be transmitted outward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-style integrations, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF caveman stores secrets or sensitive notes in its touched files
IF Haystack is configured to send retrieved context to external REST APIs or MCP-backed services
mitigations: Keep secrets out of caveman-managed files
Block Haystack egress for sensitive runs
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Review MCP server destinations before enabling retrieval
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Caveman supports multiple instances and writes files; Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers. Even without explicit shared directories, overlapping mutable surfaces via MCP or shared resources can cause write conflicts and stale state. Uncertainty remains about locking, so medium is safer than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace, git state, or MCP-backed resource
IF no external locking or optimistic concurrency control is configured
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Avoid concurrent git edits
Use per-agent MCP credentials or namespaces
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search/RAG agent that can act on retrieved content, and caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content that may be treated as authoritative. If Haystack consumes caveman output without verification, errors or injected instructions can cascade into downstream actions. Because this can affect multiple work products and defaults are not shown to verify, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF Haystack uses caveman-generated notes as source-of-truth without a verification step
IF Haystack triggers downstream actions or responses based on retrieved caveman content
mitigations: Require human review before acting on retrieved content
Add citation/grounding checks in Haystack
Mark caveman outputs as untrusted by default
Limit Haystack to read-only retrieval for this pair
requires-engineering: implement verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: Caveman touches session logs and memory files, while Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics. No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is evidenced. I do not cite both agents beyond the relevant data-handling fields because this risk is mainly about each agent’s own handling policies.
conditions: IF caveman stores regulated data in session logs or memory files
IF Haystack is configured to retain retrieved content beyond anonymous usage statistics
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in caveman files
Confirm Haystack retention settings
Document data-class boundaries for both agents
Separate compliance-sensitive workloads
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
